generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example. No parcel serviceability, broadband order state, mobile engineering coverage, network commitment or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck plan/contract/map/checker/build states against exact address-level serviceability. Planned, contracted, building, passed or forecast states remain separate from orderable service.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck currentness, contract redesign/termination, data revision and forecast dates. Later official evidence supersedes earlier programme scope or monthly management snapshots.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck national/authority/exchange/postcode evidence versus exact development address and contractual build agreement. No geographic aggregation is treated as a parcel-level result.

extra_examples.ref: Ofcom all-plans versus High Confidence separation
extra_examples.fact: Ofcom separately reports all operator deployment plans and High Confidence plans where low-level design is complete and funding committed.
extra_examples.gate: Even High Confidence remains planned deployment and not current serviceability at an address.

extra_examples.fact: The PND report projects coverage to January 2029 using plans stated as of January 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not store future projected coverage as current 2026 availability.

extra_examples.fact: Spring 2026 reports 82% residential full-fibre availability nationally.
extra_examples.gate: A national percentage gives no evidence for one parcel or development.

extra_examples.fact: Ofcom separately reports availability and take-up of full fibre.
extra_examples.gate: Network availability must not be confused with an active subscription or connected occupancy.

extra_examples.fact: Map Your Mobile reports local predicted coverage and postcode-district performance.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer exact indoor coverage for a proposed building from map coverage alone.

extra_examples.fact: Ofcom explicitly says predicted coverage cannot be 100% accurate and no signal threshold guarantees service all the time.
extra_examples.gate: Never score predicted mobile coverage as certainty.

extra_examples.fact: Crowdsourced experience complements operator predictions but represents observed user experiences across areas.
extra_examples.gate: Crowd data is not a controlled engineering survey at a development footprint.

extra_examples.fact: NPPF supports full-fibre and next-generation mobile infrastructure in development.
extra_examples.gate: Policy support does not secure a provider agreement, duct route or live service.

extra_examples.ref: Early provider engagement versus completed rights
extra_examples.fact: Government guidance encourages early developer/provider engagement and coordination.
extra_examples.gate: Engagement is not a signed access agreement, wayleave or street-works permission.

extra_examples.fact: The July release warns of variable lag between delivery and BDUK data ingestion.
extra_examples.gate: A missing or newly added count can be a reporting-timing effect rather than physical network change.

extra_examples.fact: BDUK counts contracted premises to which the supplier has delivered a gigabit-capable connection in its management information.
extra_examples.gate: A contract-level built count does not prove a particular address can order a retail service today.

extra_examples.fact: May 2026 showed built-premises reductions caused by supplier data resubmissions.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat an earlier monthly count as immutable evidence.

extra_examples.fact: January 2026 is an earlier snapshot in the same management-information series.
extra_examples.gate: Newest official management snapshot supersedes older programme counts for current context.

extra_examples.fact: BDUK says trenching, duct and fibre build precede residents/businesses requesting service from a broadband provider.
extra_examples.gate: Physical build and retail orderability are separate states.

extra_examples.fact: The 2026 redesign materially changed the contract scope after commercial rollout changed.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use the original announced footprint as current scope.

extra_examples.fact: The Kent public contract scope was substantially reduced in May 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Earlier programme inclusion does not prove continued subsidy scope or address readiness.

extra_examples.fact: The Sussex contract was redesigned after commercial network expansion.
extra_examples.gate: Commercial-overlap changes can remove premises from public scope without implying no gigabit network exists.

extra_examples.fact: The 2026 contract redesign reduced publicly funded scope.
extra_examples.gate: Reduced public scope may reflect commercial rollout and must not be interpreted as lost connectivity.

extra_examples.fact: CityFibre is no longer delivering the terminated public contract.
extra_examples.gate: Reject the terminated contract as current build evidence unless replacement/commercial address evidence exists.

extra_examples.fact: Premises moved from an incomplete Freedom Fibre arrangement into an Openreach call-off change.
extra_examples.gate: Latest supplier/contract route takes precedence over historic contract assumptions.

extra_examples.fact: The FullFibre contract terminated and the area moved into an Openreach contract change.
extra_examples.gate: Replacement programme status is still not proof of live service at an address.

extra_examples.fact: The Freedom Fibre contract was terminated and replaced by Openreach call-off eight.
extra_examples.gate: Historic supplier records cannot be counted as current delivery evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Wildanet stopped full completion of two contracts after partial delivery.
extra_examples.gate: Contracted-but-not-delivered premises require a new authoritative route before any readiness claim.

extra_examples.fact: The terminated FullFibre contract was replaced through Openreach call-off three.
extra_examples.gate: Replacement inclusion does not establish build completion or orderability.

extra_examples.fact: The public contract was redesigned from roughly 25,000 to roughly 6,000 premises.
extra_examples.gate: Programme headline quantities are not reliable parcel-level availability evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Openreach says its map is exchange-level while the postcode checker is the more personalised property view.
extra_examples.gate: Use address-level status rather than exchange colour for a target parcel.

extra_examples.fact: Openreach says planned dates can change and some smaller programmes have less certain timeframes.
extra_examples.gate: Do not store published build windows as guaranteed completion dates.

extra_examples.fact: The checker distinguishes orderable now from soon, planned and building states.
extra_examples.gate: Only the current orderable state supports live service availability.

extra_examples.fact: Openreach notes availability can differ even within the same street because build occurs in stages and access/engineering can differ.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer a site's availability from a neighbouring address.

extra_examples.fact: Openreach describes free Full Fibre infrastructure for qualifying larger new developments subject to its process and survey.
extra_examples.gate: Headline eligibility is not an accepted site design or completed installation.

extra_examples.fact: A registration is followed by a new-sites agreement/wayleave that must be returned to progress unless a framework agreement applies.
extra_examples.gate: Registration alone is not contractual acceptance.

extra_examples.fact: Openreach installs infrastructure while the new owner later orders broadband from a chosen service provider.
extra_examples.gate: Developer infrastructure completion is separate from an active retail service.

extra_examples.fact: Community partnership delivery can depend on technical survey, funding and validated pledges.
extra_examples.gate: Eligibility or expression of interest is not a committed build.

extra_examples.fact: Voucher value is released only after required build/order/installation confirmation steps.
extra_examples.gate: A pledged voucher is not proof broadband has been installed.

extra_examples.ref: Programme scale versus exact site gate
extra_examples.fact: Openreach programmes range from exchange-scale commercial builds to smaller new-site, MDU, government and community programmes.
extra_examples.gate: Programme geography/timing does not replace exact site registration and checker evidence.

extra_examples.ref: Telecom security versus physical readiness separation
extra_examples.fact: The July 2026 security code addresses risk-based provider security obligations.
extra_examples.gate: Security-governance evidence must not be treated as network coverage, capacity or build completion.
